A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AUTALIC dataset study. All 14 pages of v2 and 17 pages of v3 support comparison, including their tables and figures. v2 ends with references; v3 additionally contains Appendix A.

before.justification: v2 reports original annotation statistics, classifier evaluations, human–LLM agreement measurements, and qualitative error analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original classifier and prompting evaluations, annotation analyses, and preliminary self-agreement results in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: The proposed dataset construction and annotation procedure remains unchanged: Reddit keyword collection, surrounding context, nine annotators, three labels, and majority-based binary labels. Expanded orientation documentation does not establish a changed procedure; the new prompting comparisons concern evaluation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate anti-autistic ableist-language classification using the same final collection of 2,400 English sentences from 192 subreddits, covering 2013–2024. The keyword table is retained in v3 Appendix A.3. Added analyses do not establish additional datasets, domains, or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 evaluates GPT-4o, Llama3, Aya-23, Gemma2, Mistral, and Phi-3-Mini. v3 Table 3 removes GPT-4o, Aya, and Phi, adds DeepSeek, and introduces a reported pre-trained BERT comparator alongside fine-tuned BERT. v2 Figure 4's inconsistent 'Gemini' label prevents confidently matching that particular heatmap entry.

E3.justification: v3 adds explicit zero-shot versus in-context-learning conditions and a pre-trained versus fine-tuned BERT comparison. Reported classification metrics narrow from precision, recall, and F1 to F1. The 80%–20% splits remain. Section 3.1.1 also revises collected target/following sentence counts from 2,500 to 2,400 without changing the stated final dataset size.

E4.justification: v3 adds an analysis of whether examples improve performance and consistency across prompt wordings, four challenging annotation cases in Appendix A.5, and preliminary self-agreement analysis in A.6. Section 3.2.5 revises the disagreement analysis. Conversely, v2's model-specific safety-refusal analysis in Section 4.3.3 is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix A.6 newly reports an SD for AUTALIC annotator agreement (0.09), whereas v2 provides individual team kappas, and supplies dispersion for preliminary self-agreement. Existing model-agreement mean/SD reporting and the completion-time correlation's p-value remain. Neither version reports experimental seed counts or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Fine-tuned BERT's reported F1 changes from 0.04 in v2 Table 6 to 0.90 in v3 Table 3, which also adds pre-trained BERT at 0.43. Insufficient settings prevent treating this as a demonstrated same-setting gain. v3 adds prompt-specific and ICL scores, including DeepSeek F1 values of 0.55–0.59, replaces agreement results, and revises the disagreement passage from 59 cases to 100 posts, including 48 involving medical terminology or stereotypes.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, proofs, or mathematical derivations. Added conceptual definitions and empirical agreement statistics do not introduce mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The central claims about AUTALIC's novelty, contextual annotation, and poor human–LLM alignment remain. v3's introduction adds claims that reasoning LLMs show greater consistency across prompt terminology and that ICL provides mixed benefits. These extend the empirical claims while retaining the central dataset contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains GPT-4o's advantage through model size; v3 instead emphasizes DeepSeek's reasoning and interprets ICL as improving conceptual understanding. v3 expands discussion of individual and cultural disagreement and interprets preliminary annotation comparisons as improvement. It also claims substantial BERT fine-tuning benefits while retaining the earlier high-false-positive discussion, leaving those interpretations unreconciled.

D1.justification: v3 adds the collection month, fuller annotator-orientation materials, a platform screenshot, and password/access and reuse conditions. The full-glossary link becomes an instruction to contact the first author. However, v3 omits BERT's 335M-parameter architecture, linear classification head, test-as-validation disclosure, and earlier exact LLM variants. These documentation changes do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around comparable Reddit datasets, linguistically debatable annotation disagreements, Western dataset scope, and neurodiversity scholarship. Additions include Plank, Kapp, and DeepSeek references. It removes the Allouch studies and Kaplan scaling-law rationale. Much of Section 2 nevertheless comes from relocated introductory material rather than newly added related work.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively reorganized, dataset-label statistics move into Section 3, model subsections are consolidated, and conclusion material moves into the introduction and discussion. Annotation and ethics passages are rewritten and expanded, and a structured appendix is introduced. These are substantial narrative changes beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reformatted from a full-width illustration to a single-column display. Separate classifier tables become the grouped Table 3 with prompt-specific columns, and Figure 4 is redrawn with different labels, colors, and diagonal treatment. Keyword and glossary tables move to the appendix, which adds the self-agreement plot and annotation-interface screenshot.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful prompt-specific ICL evidence and fuller annotation documentation. However, the replacement of BERT F1 0.04 with 0.90 lacks a reproducible explanation, earlier implementation and validation disclosures disappear, and the high-false-positive discussion remains unreconciled. Its main-text annotator agreement of 0.25 also differs from Appendix A.6's 0.21 summary. These gains and unresolved reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
